title: Business financial records
log: 2026-11-04T09:36:47Z match: Claude Haiku 5.5 found no bank point the same, so it is written new

match.reason: The new point covers three statements (income statement, balance sheet and cash flow statement) at Year 8 depth, while the only close bank point teaches just the balance sheet at Year 12 depth, so it is narrower and at a different level.

draft.title: Business financial records
card: shows a business's income and expenses over a period of time, so it shows whether the business made a profit or a loss.
shows what a business owns (assets) and what it owes (liabilities) on a particular day.
shows the money that came into the business and went out of it over a period.
A business can make a profit and still run short of cash, for example if customers pay late.
draft.remember: Income statement: profit or loss. Balance sheet: owns and owes. Cash flow statement: money in and out.

a.q: Which record would show what a business owns and what it owes?
a.why: A balance sheet lists assets, which the business owns, and liabilities, which it owes. An income statement is the tempting wrong answer, because it shows profit or loss over time instead.
a.clue: Look for the record that lists assets and liabilities.

b.q: Tom's bike shop in Hobart sold many bikes in June, but customers have not yet paid. He needs to see if he can pay rent this week. Which record helps most?
b.why: Paying rent depends on money actually coming in and going out, which the cash flow statement shows. The income statement counts the June sales as income, even though the cash has not arrived, so it can look healthy while cash is short.
b.clue: Which record tracks actual money moving in and out?
